Viewers do not show an RTFD document as a text view does, and the method makes up for the differences with
A viewer takes the size of an image from the resolution of its file, not from the bounds of its attachment. The images have the resolution that makes them as large as they are in a text view.
A viewer ignores the vertical offset of an attachment, which is what keeps a formula within a line aligned with the text. The offset is stored as the attribute
, which the format keeps.
A viewer does not make an image smaller if it is wider than the page, so
limits the width of diagrams and formulas. Its default, 400 points, fits into a page of the size US Letter or A4 with margins of one inch, also within lists and block quotes.

that takes a string understands
(the upper and lower edge, and the left and right edge) and

(the upper, right, lower and left edge, as in CSS). A page is broken between lines of text, not through them. A list item, a code block or a row of a table moves to the next page as a whole if it fits on a page, and a heading is not the last line of a page. Only a block that is taller than a page is broken. The text is about 70% as large as in the other formats (14 points become about 10 points), and so are formulas, because the text of a page is smaller than the text of a view; the rendering option

scales it further. All diagrams are scaled by the same factor, which makes a diagram of the width that Mermaid draws for (800 points) as wide as the text of a page (0.56 for A4): a diagram that is wider than another one on the page has the same size of text, and the text of diagrams is a little smaller than the text of the document. The importer which creates the text does not make fonts smaller than 9 points, so the text of a page is never smaller, whatever the style says.

The text is black by default, whatever the appearance of the system is (see the style below). The numbers and bullets of lists sit on the baseline of the first line of their items. Links are clickable: each line of a link is an area that opens its URL (links to a place in the same document,
, are not).
